gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ the rooms in the hotel have a sea view; the rest face the car park.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the rooms' a partitive is needed: Some of; 'all/none' contradict the context.

gaps.sentence: Have we got ___ eggs for breakfast?
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in neutral questions; 'none' cannot stand before a noun.
